questions.question: What does the class selector select?
options: All elements with a specific id attribute
All elements with a specific class attribute
All elements of a specific type
questions.explanation: The class selector (.) selects all elements with a specific class attribute. For example, .intro selects all elements with class="intro".

questions.question: What is the correct syntax for a class selector?
questions.explanation: Class selectors use a period (.) followed by the class name. For example, .intro selects elements with class="intro".

questions.question: What is the correct syntax for an ID selector?
questions.explanation: ID selectors use a hash (#) followed by the ID name. For example, #firstname selects the element with id="firstname".

questions.question: What does the universal selector (*) select?
questions.explanation: The universal selector (*) selects all elements on the page. It's useful for applying styles to everything or resetting default styles.

questions.question: What does the selector 'div p' (with a space) select?
options:
All

elements that are direct children of

elements
questions.explanation:
The space between selectors creates a descendant selector. 'div p' selects all

elements that are inside

elements, at any nesting level.

element (child selector)

elements where the parent is a

element (direct children only, not grandchildren).

questions.explanation:
The + symbol creates an adjacent sibling selector. 'div + p' selects all

elements that are placed immediately after

elements (next sibling).

Every

    element (they share the same parent).

questions.question:
Consider this CSS:
```css
h1, h2, h3 { color: red; }
```

What does this selector do?
options: Selects h1 elements inside h2 elements inside h3 elements
Applies the same rule to h1, h2, and h3 elements (grouping selectors)
Selects h3 elements that are siblings of h2 elements that are siblings of h1 elements
questions.explanation: The comma groups selectors together. This rule applies the same styles (color: red) to all h1, h2, and h3 elements. This is called grouping selectors.

questions.question:
Consider this HTML: ```html

Paragraph 1

Paragraph 2

``` Which selector would select BOTH paragraphs?
questions.explanation:
The descendant selector 'div p' (with a space) selects all

elements inside

elements at any nesting level, so it would select both paragraphs. 'div > p' would only select the first paragraph (direct child).

questions.question: What is an element selector?
options: A selector that uses a class name
A selector that uses an ID name
A selector that selects elements based on the element name
A selector that uses the universal *
questions.explanation:
An element selector selects elements based on the element name. For example, 'h1' selects all

elements, and 'p' selects all

elements.
